clue.text: Atmosphere surrounding son and woman

indicators.note: the atmosphere word goes round the outside of the son letter, enclosing it

parts.note: the ether is the upper air, the atmosphere
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A mood or air hangs around a boy and a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts S inside ETHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a female given name, and a biblical queen, so any woman of that name fits.

clue.text: Land by crashing into sea

indicators.note: crashing suggests things smashing apart, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Something lands by crashing into the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic country, and a country is a land.

clue.text: Model's tall, showing bit of leg

parts.note: the Model T was Ford's famous early car
high means tall

explanation.surface: A tall fashion model shows a little leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T, Ford's famous car, supplies the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper part of the leg between hip and knee is one section of it.

clue.text: Private lives: topless sex club's regulars drunk

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and confused, so these letters are jumbled
topless means the top letter is removed from the word sex
regulars are the letters at regular intervals, every other one of club

explanation.surface: Private lives of regulars at a topless sex club who are drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' cuts SEX to EX; 'regulars' takes CU from CLUB; 'drunk' rearranges LIVES + EX + CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusive means restricted to a select few, so closed to the public, private.

clue.text: Did kiss with lots of activity in bed

indicators.note: the activity word is placed inside the bed word, sitting within it

parts.note: taken as written
a rush is a burst of busy, hurried activity

explanation.surface: Someone kissed amid a flurry of energetic goings-on in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The saucy surface makes 'Did kiss' look tame beside the bed; the light touch of lips is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush lips with someone is to give a light kiss, so the past tense fits 'did kiss'.

clue.text: Bowled with field around me: one that's driven is caught here?

definitions.text: one that's driven is caught here?

indicators.note: the bowled and field letters go around the me word, enclosing it

parts.note: B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
to field a ball in cricket is to stop it
us is northern English dialect for me

explanation.surface: A cricketer is bowled with fielders placed round him, and the drive gets caught.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a drive is a shot and a catch dismisses the batter; here the thing driven is a bus, and passengers catch it.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a vehicle that is driven and that passengers catch at a roadside stopping place.

clue.text: One pub that's free

parts.note: un is French for one, also dialect 'un' for one
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub that serves for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbar a door is to remove its bolt, setting it loose, the verb sense of freeing.

clue.text: They might run around a lawn with rackets? Cash ultimately with advantage first

definitions.text: They might run around a lawn

indicators.note: the cash and advantage letters come first, ahead of the rackets word
ultimately means in the end, so the final letter of cash is taken

parts.note: an edge is an advantage
rows are noisy disturbances, rackets

explanation.surface: Tennis rackets around a lawn, with cash and advantage mattering most.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis words (lawn, rackets, advantage) disguise rackets as din.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines of shrubs bordering gardens and fields can run around the edge of a lawn.

clue.text: Mafia boss had to chip in

parts.note: a don is the head of a Mafia family
to have a meal is to eat it, so had means ate

explanation.surface: The Mafia boss was forced to contribute.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is to contribute money to a shared cause, as a donor gives.

clue.text: Maybe press name central figure

parts.note: the press is an example of the media, hence maybe

explanation.surface: The newspapers might name someone as the key person.
explanation.definitionFit: In statistics the middle value of an ordered set is the central number.

clue.text: Cuckoo with crest? They'll be excited

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters of these words are scrambled

explanation.surface: Seeing a crested cuckoo will thrill people who look for rare birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' rearranges WITH CREST. The bird surface is apt: the answer is also slang for keen birdwatchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that twitch are jumpy and agitated; the word also names birders who rush excitedly after rare sightings.

clue.text: Wait to get new president

parts.note: to bide is to wait, as in biding one's time

explanation.surface: Be patient and you will get a fresh head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Biden was the 46th President of the United States.

clue.text: Republican female reflected: 'Trump essentially a one-time leader'

indicators.note: as in a mirror, the Republican and female letters are read backwards

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican in US politics
a hen is a female bird

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the central letter of Trump is taken

explanation.surface: A Republican woman looks back and calls Trump, at heart, a former leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns R + HEN into NEHR; 'essentially' takes U, the middle of TRUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, a national leader of the past.

clue.text: Cross from wing with Italian team taking the lead

indicators.note: the Italian team goes in front, so its letters come first in the answer

parts.note: Inter Milan is a famous Italian football club, called Inter for short
a wing of a party or church is a faction, a sect

explanation.surface: An Italian side scores from a cross on the wing to go ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface makes 'Cross' look like a pass from the wing; it is a verb meaning to meet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that cross meet and pass through each other, which is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Here trade union breaking up conflict

indicators.note: the union letter breaks into the conflict word, splitting it apart

parts.note: action is fighting, as in soldiers seeing action

explanation.surface: A trade union is breaking up a dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking up' puts U inside ACTION. 'trade union' reads as one phrase but splits: 'Here trade' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale by bidding is a place or event where goods change hands, so it is where trading happens.

clue.text: With fluctuations of fortune, order to move money on roulette bet?

indicators.note: in a down clue the roulette word sits on, so below, the money word

parts.note: a cheque is a written order to a bank to pay money
red is one of the colour bets at roulette

explanation.surface: Writing a cheque to put money on a roulette bet, with fortunes swinging.
explanation.definitionFit: A chequered career or history is one marked by ups and downs, good and bad luck.

clue.text: Detective with details about ordinary victim

parts.note: PI is a private investigator

indicators.note: the details word goes around the ordinary letter, enclosing it

parts.note: gen is British slang for information or details
O is an abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: An investigator gathers facts about an ordinary victim of crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang a pigeon is a dupe, someone easily swindled, as in stool pigeon or a mark for cheats.

clue.text: Billed one with German antique clock

parts.note: olden means of times long past, ancient
to clock is slang for seeing or noticing, to eye

explanation.surface: An invoiced item: one antique German clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' is slang for noticing, so EYE.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldeneye is a diving duck, and a duck is a bird with a bill.

clue.text: Concerning this love, female after present

indicators.note: the love and female letters come after the present word in the answer

parts.note: to be here is to be present
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A love affair, with a woman coming along after the gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts O + F behind HERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal legal adverb meaning of or about this document or matter.

clue.text: Blonde to approach best place for swingers?

parts.note: fair hair is blonde hair
a way is an approach or means of access

explanation.surface: A blonde goes up to a spot ideal for swingers.
explanation.walkthrough: The swingers are golfers, not partner-swappers.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the mown strip between tee and green is the ideal lie for a golfer's swing.

clue.text: Pubs struggling over complete mess

indicators.note: the shuffled pub letters spread over the whole word, enclosing it
struggling suggests something in disarray, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: complete means all, entire

explanation.surface: Bars in difficulty have become a total shambles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges PUBS to BSUP.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a botched job or a fiasco, a muddle.

clue.text: Horn working for racing driver

parts.note: to horn is to butt with horns
on means working or operating, as a switched-on machine

explanation.surface: A car horn functions for a racer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horn' is a verb here: to gore or ram with horns.
explanation.definitionFit: Jenson Button is a British driver who won the 2009 Formula One world title.

clue.text: Lace set in short knickers, like one hanging in there

indicators.note: the lace word is set inside the shortened knickers word
short means cut, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: pants are British underwear, knickers
to lace a shoe is to tie it

explanation.surface: Lace put into skimpy knickers, sexy lingerie for someone holding on.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is the British word for knickers; cut short it becomes PANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone hanging in there bears hardship calmly without giving up, showing forbearance.

clue.text: Remove organ from dead sailor first

indicators.note: the sailor letters come first, before the dead word

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
the late person is someone who has died

explanation.surface: Take out the organs from the dead sailor first.
explanation.definitionFit: In surgery, ablation is cutting away body tissue, so the verb means to excise part of the body.

clue.text: Model is erotic type

parts.note: blue means risqué or pornographic, as in a blue movie
print is printed type, as in small print

explanation.surface: A model is an erotic sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan or template to work from is a model, as with a technical drawing.

clue.text: Model in advert having no time

indicators.note: having no means the time letter is taken out of the advert word

parts.note: a poster is a printed advertisement

explanation.surface: A model in an advertisement has no time to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no' removes T from POSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who poses for an artist or photographer sits as a model.

clue.text: Green on back of course to turn outwards

indicators.note: the green word is put on, so after, the course letter
the back of a word is its final letter, here of course

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: On a golf green at the far end of the course, something is twisted outward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' takes E from COURSE; 'on' puts VERT after it. Vert is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy and surgery, everting an eyelid or organ means turning it inside out.

clue.text: Woman who sinned spread over magazine to excite

indicators.note: the woman's name is spread over the magazine, wrapping around it

parts.note: Eve ate the forbidden fruit in Genesis
OK! is a British celebrity magazine

explanation.surface: Eve sprawls over a magazine to arouse interest.
explanation.walkthrough: OK! is a British celebrity magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke feelings or memories is to stir them up, to arouse them.

clue.text: Loads of room in a short top

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the last letter is lost

parts.note: a crest is the top of a hill or wave

explanation.surface: There's plenty of space inside a cropped T-shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts T from CREST.
explanation.definitionFit: Acres are units of land area, and the plural colloquially means lots of space.

clue.text: Clean ladies mostly tackling pores

indicators.note: to tackle is to grapple with, taken here as wrapping round the pores word
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ladies are women
pores are tiny holes in the skin

explanation.surface: Women, for the most part, attack their pores to get clean skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' leaves WOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean in the moral sense, as in clean fun, means healthy and decent.

clue.text: Old tree, leafy on both sides

parts.note: the elder is a small tree with white flowers and berries

indicators.note: the two sides of the word leafy are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An aged tree, with foliage on either side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on both sides' takes L and Y from LEAFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on in years is a polite synonym for being aged.

clue.text: Not completely nude — centrefold's wearing clothes!

indicators.note: only part of the words is shown, so the letters are found inside them

explanation.surface: A centrefold model isn't quite naked, as she has something on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not completely' points to letters running across NUDE and CENTREFOLD. 'Not completely nude' looks like the definition; the definition is 'wearing clothes'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking 'are you decent?' means are you dressed enough to be seen.
